extracted.intended_audience: Nonprofit leaders, prospective grantees, partners, and philanthropic practitioners interested in urban grantmaking and Kresge Foundation funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing Kresge Foundation's approach to funding work that expands equity and opportunity in U.S. cities, including program priorities, geographic focus, funding instruments, and preferred models of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on cities (rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: We Focus on Cities Because They… Are powerful vehicles of change; Offer a concentration of the skills and ideas needed to spark innovation; Have a density of assets that contribute to expanded opportunity; Are manageable units of governance; Are open to engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kresge prioritizes cities as the primary unit for impact because of their capacity for innovation, concentration of assets and governance structures that enable engagement and change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-program strategic intersections to expand equity and opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Kresge works strategically to find the intersections between eight programs and practices to expand equity and opportunity in America’s cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that crosses program boundaries and leverages multiple program/practice areas to advance equitable opportunity rather than siloed single-program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic approach: deep place-based work plus national funding
rubrics_metrics.description: We work deeply in places like Detroit, Fresno, Memphis and New Orleans. We also fund work nationally, to improve systems and advance equitable policies nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding strategy combines concentrated, long-term place-based investment in select focus cities with complementary national-level grants and policy/system change efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible funding instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: We use an array of flexible grantmaking and social investment tools, including general operating support, project grants, planning grants and impact investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kresge values flexible supports (e.g., general operating support) and a mix of traditional grants and investment vehicles to meet partner needs and leverage impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote effective, inclusive community development practices
rubrics_metrics.description: We promote effective, inclusive community development practices in U.S. cities, especially New Orleans, Memphis and Fresno.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority for initiatives that advance inclusive community development approaches—practices that center inclusion and effectiveness in urban contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts & Culture as drivers of just communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Arts & Culture: We position culture and creativity as drivers of more just communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for cultural and creative activities framed as catalysts for justice and community well-being, rather than solely aesthetic or commercial goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering resident priorities and cross-sector collaboration (Detroit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detroit: We collaborate cross-sectorally to promote and expand long-term, equitable opportunity in Kresge’s hometown by centering the priorities of its residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective proposals should demonstrate resident-centered approaches and cross-sector partnerships that aim for durable, equitable outcomes in Detroit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education: increase postsecondary attainment and eliminate equity gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Education: We work to increase postsecondary attainment while eliminating equity gaps in the U.S. and South Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding interest in programs that both raise attainment and explicitly address equity gaps, including work with international (South Africa) partners where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment: climate action that advances racial and economic justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment: We help cities combat and adapt to climate change while advancing racial and economic justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should integrate climate mitigation/adaptation with strategies that center racial and economic justice rather than treating climate as separate from equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health: building equity-focused systems of health
rubrics_metrics.description: Health: We help build equity-focused systems of health that create opportunities for all people to achieve well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for systemic health interventions designed to reduce disparities and expand well-being for all populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Services: accelerate social and economic mobility for people with low incomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Services: We accelerate social and economic mobility for people with low incomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs targeting measurable increases in mobility for low-income populations are aligned with Kresge priorities in human services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Investment Practice: break down barriers to capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Social Investment Practice: We work across the seven program areas in U.S. cities to breakdown barriers to capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investment-oriented work should focus on improving capital access and financing structures that enable equitable urban development across program areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort/Initiative funding model with shared learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives: Grants or investments are awarded in a cohort model, often with common activities, a shared learning goal and/or convening opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kresge often funds through cohort-based initiatives that emphasize shared activities, collective learning, and convening; prospective partners should be prepared for collaborative timelines and learning expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity-focused capacity building (LIFT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership Infrastructure and Funding Team (LIFT): LIFT uses an equity lens to strengthen our partners’ leadership and the nonprofit sector through capacity-building grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity-building proposals that explicitly apply an equity lens to strengthen leadership and organizational infrastructure are a fit for LIFT resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to learning & evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning & Evaluation: We are committed to strategic learning and knowledge sharing that advance our mission and the fields in which we work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees and partners are expected to engage in strategic learning, data collection, evaluation and knowledge-sharing aligned with program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus cities: prioritized programs and translating lessons across places
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus Cities: Kresge works nationally and with a special focus in certain cities. Since 2015, we have worked with local leaders to translate lessons from Detroit to Memphis and advance equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for locally rooted partnerships and for projects that can translate and adapt lessons between cities to accelerate equitable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priorities in Fresno (cross-sector planning, organizing, advocacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fresno: Since 2018, we’ve sought to expand equity and opportunity by funding cross-sector planning and collaboration, community and economic development, community organizing, and advocacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Fresno, Kresge favors cross-sector planning/collaboration and community-driven organizing, development and advocacy efforts that drive equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-departmental and collaborative internal funding approach
rubrics_metrics.description: While each program or practice funds work individually, we also work frequently through cross-team collaborations, by funding initiatives (cohorts of partners working on a common work plan), and through internal, cross-department funding teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note Kresge's internal collaboration across programs; projects that align with multiple program priorities or that invite cross-departmental engagement may be advantaged.
